projects.title: Integrated Watershed Development Programme
projects.description: Construction of 142 check dams, 87 farm ponds, and 23 rock-fill dams across 12 villages — recharging groundwater for over 4,500 farming households.
projects.longDescription: The Integrated Watershed Development Programme was executed across 12 water-stressed villages in the semi-arid Rayalaseema belt. Through hydrological topography mapping, continuous soil conservation, and participatory ridge-to-valley interventions, this initiative restored ecological equilibrium, elevated groundwater levels, and secured year-round agricultural water supply for drought-prone farming communities.
projects.beneficiaries: 4,500+ small & marginal farming households across 12 village panchayats
projects.approach: Ridge-to-valley hydrological planning combined with community-led construction and social audits.
objectives: Harvest runoff rainwater and recharge deep aquifers through decentralized civil structures
Prevent severe topsoil erosion on over 22,000 acres of agricultural and community wasteland
Increase double-cropping area and drought resilience among smallholder farmers
Empower local Watershed User Associations for enduring community governance
highlights: 142 check dams and 87 farm ponds constructed
23 rock-fill dams and 310 percolation trenches installed
Groundwater table rose by an average of 4.2 meters across project clusters
Crop productivity increased by 38% for groundnut, pulses, and millets
projects.imageAlt: Watershed landscape with community water project

projects.title: Farmer Producer Organization (FPO) Promotion
projects.description: Mobilized 3,200 smallholder farmers into 4 FPOs, providing market linkages, post-harvest infrastructure and access to institutional credit.
projects.longDescription: Small and marginal farmers often face severe exploitation in commodity markets due to fragmented yields and middleman monopolies. Our FPO promotion project organizes farming communities into registered, professionally governed collective enterprises, equipping them with bulk input purchasing power, organic certifications, processing hubs, and direct institutional buyer networks.
projects.beneficiaries: 3,200+ smallholder & tribal farmers across dryland districts
projects.approach: Village-level mobilization, democratic cooperative governance, value-chain infrastructure, and buyer tie-ups.
objectives: Aggregate farm produce to negotiate premium market prices and eliminate exploitative intermediaries
Establish decentralized cleaning, grading, packing, and solar-drying facilities
Transition 1,200+ acres to climate-resilient natural farming and indigenous millets
Facilitate institutional working capital and low-interest crop credit linkages
highlights: 4 registered, self-sustaining FPOs operating with professional management
₹4.8 Crore cumulative turnover achieved across pulses, millets, and groundnuts
Direct farm-gate price realization improved by 22-30% for member farmers
Established 2 modern primary processing and value-addition centers
projects.imageAlt: Farmers working together in a field

projects.title: Women-led Nutrition Gardens
projects.description: Supported women’s collectives to build kitchen gardens, improve family nutrition and increase income through vegetable sales.
projects.longDescription: Combating chronic micronutrient deficiencies and seasonal food insecurity, this initiative equips rural women with heirloom non-GMO seeds, bio-manure techniques, and micro-drip irrigation setups to transform backyard spaces into productive organic kitchen gardens, improving health indicators and family self-reliance.
projects.approach: Self-Help Group (SHG) aggregation, bio-intensive permaculture training, and seed bank creation.
objectives: Ensure dietary diversity and year-round access to fresh, pesticide-free greens and vegetables
Reduce out-of-pocket household expenditures on essential groceries
Generate supplemental household income through local weekly market sales of surplus produce
Foster women's financial autonomy and leadership within village Gram Sabhas
highlights: 1,850+ individual and 45 community nutrition gardens established
Over 65% reduction in child anaemia rates recorded across target project hamlets
Participating women generated an additional ₹3,000–₹5,000 monthly from surplus sales
Trained 120 women as certified community organic farming trainers (Krishi Sakhis)
projects.imageAlt: Women tending a small vegetable garden

projects.title: Child Rights Learning Circles
projects.description: Established child-friendly learning circles to promote rights awareness, school retention and safe spaces for marginalized children.
projects.longDescription: Targeting high-dropout rural corridors, Child Rights Learning Circles provide safe, creative after-school learning environments. Through remedial education, life-skills sessions, child protection committees, and anti-child marriage advocacy, we ensure that every child's right to education, protection, and childhood is vigilantly defended.
projects.approach: Community-based learning centers, peer mentors, parent counseling, and police/panchayat convergence.
objectives: Prevent school dropouts, child labour, and child marriage in vulnerable habitations
Provide foundational literacy, numeracy, and STEM-based interactive learning
Establish Village Child Protection Committees (VCPCs) in collaboration with local schools
Provide psychosocial counseling and scholarship support for higher education
highlights: 32 active Learning Circles operating 6 days a week
Zero child marriages recorded in adopted intervention hamlets over the past 3 years
94% primary-to-secondary school retention rate achieved
140+ dropouts successfully mainstreamed back into formal government schools

projects.title: Community Health and Nutrition Outreach
projects.description: Delivered village health camps, nutrition counselling, and maternal care guidance to strengthen wellbeing across remote communities.
projects.longDescription: Bridging the critical last-mile healthcare gap in remote villages with limited primary healthcare access, this programme deploys mobile healthcare teams, preventative health screenings, telemedicine linkages, and intensive maternal and newborn care monitoring.
projects.beneficiaries: 8,200+ rural residents, with special focus on expectant mothers and seniors
projects.approach: Door-to-door health surveillance, mobile diagnostic camps, and collaboration with ASHA/Anganwadi workers.
objectives: Deliver comprehensive primary diagnostics, essential medicines, and specialist doctor consultations
Screen for non-communicable diseases (hypertension, diabetes) and early maternal risks
Distribute nutritional supplements and conduct balanced diet cooking demonstrations
Enable seamless referral linkages with district and tertiary government hospitals
highlights: 48 multi-specialty mobile health camps conducted reaching 8,200+ patients
1,200+ pregnant and lactating mothers supported through regular nutritional monitoring
100% institutional deliveries achieved among registered expectant mothers
Distributed 5,000+ preventative health and hygiene kits
